ai.ocrDpiHelp: Pages are rendered at this resolution for OCR. 200 DPI gave the best results on our tests; try 300–400 for very small print.
ai.ocrHowToTitle: How to install the OCR models
ai.ocrHowToStep1: Click “Get file” on both models above. Your browser downloads them from Qvault’s GitHub release; the app itself does not connect.
ai.ocrHowToStep2: Keep both files in the same folder, with their original names.
ai.ocrHowToStep3: Optional: check each SHA-256 below (macOS/Linux: shasum -a 256 <file>; Windows: certutil -hashfile <file> SHA256). Qvault also verifies them on import.
ai.ocrHowToStep4: Click “Import from file” and select both files.
ai.ocrHowToAirGapped: Offline or air-gapped computer? Download the files on another machine and copy them over on removable media, then import them here.
ai.embeddingModelsDesc: Suggests groups of name variants across documents. Without it, grouping uses spelling rules, which measured almost as well.
ai.embeddingToggle: Use it to suggest groups of name variants

ai.embeddingNotInstalled: Not installed: entity grouping uses spelling rules only.
ai.embeddingOff: Turned off: entity grouping uses spelling rules only.
ai.embeddingEngineUnavailable: AI engine unavailable: entity grouping uses spelling rules only.

modelNotes.openai_privacy_filter_int8: Fast on any computer (well under a second per page without a GPU). Finds names, addresses, dates, contact details and account-style numbers; company names, amounts and case numbers stay with the rules (and the language model, if you also run it).
modelNotes.qwen3_0_6b_q8_0: For computers with little memory: finds less than the default model.
modelNotes.qwen3_4b_q4_k_m: Finds more, about twice as slow as the default. Best with 16 GB of memory or a GPU.
modelNotes.qwen3_8b_q4_k_m: Highest recall in the eval, about 3.5× slower than the default. Needs a GPU workstation.
modelNotes.qwen2_5_0_5b_instruct_q4_k_m: Superseded by Qwen3 0.6B, which finds more and is faster.
modelNotes.nomic_embed_text_v2_moe_q8_0: Optional. Adds similarity-based suggestions when grouping name variants; grouping works without it.

learning.intro: Qvault remembers what you approve and reject. Text you rejected before is still shown when it appears again, marked and listed last, so you can reject it in one click. Only text you put on the “Not personal data” list is left out of future scans, and every scan says how many findings it set aside.
learning.storage: Your decisions and this list are stored unencrypted in the app data folder on this computer, like your documents and review history. Nothing leaves the computer.
learning.removed: Removed from the list. Future scans will flag it again.
learning.candidatesHint: You rejected these several times and never approved them. Nothing is added unless you click.
learning.listHint: Exact texts (ignoring case, accents and spacing) that future scans leave out for the given type. Share it with your firm by exporting and importing the file.
learning.previewSkipped_one: {{count}} item is already on your list and will be skipped.
learning.previewSkipped_other: {{count}} items are already on your list or repeated and will be skipped.
learning.previewInvalid_one: {{count}} item is invalid and will be skipped:
learning.previewInvalid_other: {{count}} items are invalid and will be skipped:
learning.empty: The list is empty. Add items here, from a suggestion, or with “Never flag this again” on a rejected finding.
learning.newPlaceholder: Text that is not personal data, e.g. “Effective Date”
learning.memoryHint: Used to mark findings you rejected before and to suggest list items. Approvals are forgotten when you delete their document; rejections are kept until you clear them here.
learning.forgetConfirm: Forget all remembered review decisions? Your “Not personal data” list is kept.
